features.statement: Page has exactly one h1 containing the site name, with a clear heading hierarchy of h2 section titles and h3 item titles.
Testimonials use blockquote, cite and figure elements, and the footer contact info uses an address element.
Photos are shown as CSS background images rather than img elements.
Intro sits below the hero in a two-column about layout instead of over a photo.
Contained content sections alternate with full-bleed photo or colored bands spanning the full viewport width.
Layout relies on CSS grid for multi-column sections, alongside flexbox.
Testimonials appear as several side-by-side white cards with orange star ratings, with no raw schema data exposed.
Blog posts appear as a 2×2 grid of bordered cream rounded cards with left-aligned titles and sentence-case bylines.
Social links are uniform outlined white pill buttons rather than brand-colored widget tiles.
Calls to action are fully rounded pill buttons in an accent color.
Small uppercase letter-spaced accent-colored eyebrow labels sit above headings.
Copy adds extra sections and CTAs with short, friendly microcopy such as 'More happy clients' and 'Visit the blog'.
Bio copy is broken into a heading, an italic serif pull line and link cards, with a punchy hero tagline.
Typography pairs a clean sans body font with an expressive serif display font for headings.
Headings are large and semibold, with a very large hero h1 and a bigger h2 scale.
Body text is about 17px with generous line height.
Page background is a warm cream with dark brown text rather than pure white and black.
Accent color is a pinkish crimson/magenta used for buttons, text accents and key heading words.
Footer is dark near-black with light text, arranged in three columns with small muted disclosure text.
Dark overlay tints and gradients are applied over photo backgrounds, with white text on top.
Separation uses thin borders on cards and section edges instead of hr dividers.
Nav links are light-weight white text over the hero photo, with no distinct active-state color.
Underlines are limited to inline text links and footer; cards, buttons and nav links are not underlined.
Markup is lean and hand-authored, with few class tokens, few inline styles, and sections instead of articles.
Page is compact and short, with less content and lower word count.
